## Context / Problem
Revise the completed verbosity research after user correction. The original ten deterministic signals were not merely unvalidated: the historical calibration refuted them as production recommendations. The final guidance must be artifact-specific, and any replacement deterministic rule or LLM criterion must show a positive effect on the historical ticket corpus before recommendation.

## Approach
- Scope writing guidance separately for executable ticket descriptions/plans, ticket comments/handoffs, ADRs, user-facing documentation, reference/API documentation, incident/security records, and session logs/research notes.
- Treat unchosen alternatives as inappropriate in an executable ticket once a path is chosen, but retain considered alternatives and decision rationale in an ADR.
- Give user-facing documentation its own contract for task-oriented explanation, examples, troubleshooting, and progressive disclosure.
- Remove “owner” from the fresh-agent resumption check; test only current state, chosen path, constraints, proof, blocker, and exact next action.
- Explicitly classify all ten calibration-v1 rules as refuted for production use. Do not describe zero-positive results as useful signals, and do not recommend any signal with false positives greater than or equal to true positives.
- Mine the frozen 20-ticket sample for new, precisely defined candidate signals. Compute TP/FP/FN/TN for each candidate against the existing adjudicated labels. Recommend only candidates with TP > 0 and TP > FP, while clearly distinguishing retrospective discovery from held-out validation.
- Record the correction, artifact-scoped guidance, candidate definitions, measurements, limitations, and next validation requirements in the linked session_log.

## Artifacts
- Updated research in session_log 59a7-cb88-f2f9-4148.
- Updated calibration findings and final answer.
- No repository files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Guidance has separate named sections for all seven artifact classes listed in the Approach.
- [x] The executable-ticket section excludes unchosen alternatives after selection.
- [x] The ADR section requires considered alternatives and the reason for rejection.
- [x] The user-facing-documentation section covers task explanation, examples, troubleshooting, and progressive disclosure.
- [x] “Owner” is absent from the fresh-agent resumption check.
- [x] The result identifies each of R1–R10 as refuted for production use and withdraws it.
- [x] Each newly proposed signal states an executable detector definition.
- [x] Each newly proposed signal reports TP, FP, FN, and TN on the frozen 20-ticket corpus.
- [x] Each newly proposed signal has TP > 0 and TP > FP on that corpus.
- [x] The result labels same-sample findings “retrospective discovery,” not held-out validation or an enforcement basis.
- [x] The result specifies the held-out validation required before production use.
- [x] Session log 59a7-cb88-f2f9-4148 contains the corrected research and is named in the artifact list.
- [x] Repository-file diff remains empty for this task.

## Verification
Candidate detectors were rerun over the frozen 20-ticket corpus. A background reviewer independently re-fetched all 20 tickets through MCP and reproduced the three signal matrices and their union. The corrected session_log was inspected after append; no repository files were modified.
